research_rationale: Whole-lifecycle YES claim for EO 11593 (Protection and Enhancement of the Cultural Environment, May 13, 1971, 36 FR 8921), read in full from the held Federal Register text after correcting the packet inventory, which began at section 2(a) and used duplicate-labelled scopes, to the 17 separately decided commands of sections 1, 2 and 3. Every command is a standing duty of federal agencies or the Secretary of the Interior. The dated paragraphs, 2(a) (by July 1, 1973) and 2(e) (by January 1, 1972 and annually thereafter), are deadlines, not ends, and paragraph 2(b) is applied today: the held current 36 CFR 63.1 says the Interior regulations explain determinations of eligibility under section 2(b) of the order and implement sections 1(3) and 2(b), and 36 CFR parts 60, 63 and 68 and many other eCFR parts name the order as of 2026-10-14. No later instrument amending, revoking or superseding it is held (the chain is empty; EO 13006 and EO 13022 recite it without changing it). The U.S. Code edition is current through 2026-10-09; that limit is stated, not filled.
savings_reason: The order remains in force in full; no clause terminated and the held eCFR text, packet chain and OFR catalog search show no ending, so no savings or residual effect arises.
earlier_end_check: No earlier end exists: the order has no own-terms end; the dated paragraphs 2(a) and 2(e) are deadlines, not ends, and 2(e) continues annually; no held instrument amends, revokes or supersedes any paragraph.
scope_check: Seventeen scopes are decided separately (section 1, lead-ins and paragraphs of sections 2 and 3); none is partially revoked or amended in any held source, and the corrected inventory replaces the packet scopes that omitted section 1.
independent_command_check: The agency duties in section 2 and the Secretary of the Interior duties in section 3 are independent standing commands; the dated paragraphs were not one-time commands exhausted by performance because they identify and nominate qualifying properties as they arise, submit procedures annually, and are applied through 36 CFR 63.1.
savings_check: Nothing ended, so no savings or residual question arises: every section and paragraph continues.

research_rationale: Whole-lifecycle YES claim for EO 12448 (Exercise of Authority Under Section 218 of Title 18, United States Code, November 4, 1983, 48 FR 51281), read in full from the held Federal Register text. Section 1 delegates to the head of each executive department, military department and executive agency the President's authority under 18 U.S.C. 218 to declare void and rescind transactions after a final conviction for a violation of chapter 11 of title 18. Section 2 lets those heads exercise the authority by regulation and requires the Secretary of Defense, the Administrator of General Services and the Administrator of the National Aeronautics and Space Administration jointly to issue government-wide implementing regulations on voiding or rescinding contracts. Section 3 and its paragraphs (a) to (d) fix the minimum procedural protections every implementing regulation must give (written notice, an opportunity to submit information, a hearing on request, and a written final decision stating restitution). The order has no date, expiry or condition and no revocation or supersession of another order. No later instrument amending or ending it is held: the packet chain has no events and the later-events OFR catalog search recorded 0 disposition notes. The current eCFR text of 48 CFR 3.703, held as a lead from the eCFR search as of 2026-10-14, still describes the order as the delegation of the President's authority under 18 U.S.C. 218, and the U.S. Code prints the order as a note to 18 U.S.C. 218 without an ending statement. The U.S. Code edition is current through 2026-10-09; that limit is stated, not filled.
savings_reason: The order remains in force in full; no clause has terminated and the held U.S. Code, eCFR lead, packet chain and OFR catalog search show no ending, so no savings or residual effect arises.
earlier_end_check: No earlier end exists: the order has no own-terms end, no later instrument is held that amends, revokes or supersedes it, and the OFR catalog search recorded no disposition note. The joint-regulation requirement in section 2 is a standing proviso to the exercise of the delegated authority, not a report deadline or one-time task with a date, so it is not treated as an end.
scope_check: Sections 1, 2 and 3 and paragraphs 3(a) to 3(d) are decided separately. No source partially revokes or amends any of them. The inventory (seven scopes) covers every operative command in the order; there is no savings or exception clause.
independent_command_check: Section 2 (implementing regulations, joint government-wide regulations) and section 3 (minimum procedures) are independent continuing commands attached to the section 1 delegation; none was a one-time act that exhausted itself, because the implementing regulations are standing rules (48 CFR 3.703 still refers to the delegation) and section 3 limits every regulation adopted under the order.
savings_check: Nothing ended, so no savings or residual question arises: the delegation, the regulation-making command and the procedural minimums all continue; the order has no savings clause and no held instrument preserves or transfers anything.

research_rationale: Whole-lifecycle YES claim for EO 11085 (The Presidential Medal of Freedom, February 22, 1963, 28 FR 1759), read in full from the held Federal Register text after splitting the packet inventory (four mixed scopes) into twelve separately decided commands. The order is mostly an amendment of EO 9586: section 1 rewrote its numbered sections and section 2 amended EO 10717. EO 11515 (1970-03-13) substituted subsection 2(b) and struck all numbered sections other than 1 and 2, so the Board sections ended on that date while the Medal itself and the award provisions survive; EO 12014 (1977-10-19) abolished the Board, after those clauses had ended. The two amendment clauses (the section 1 lead-in and section 2(a)) are self-executing and ended on signing, 1963-02-22. Section 2(b) of the order (existing arrangements continue) is operative. The U.S. Code edition is current through 2026-10-09; the held record contains no current-law text that names this order, so the claim rests on the absence of an ending in the bounded searches and in the held chain.
savings_reason: The order remains in force in part: the Medal sections continue, the Board sections ended 1970-03-13 and the amendment clauses were exhausted on signing 1963-02-22; no separate savings residual is claimed.
earlier_end_check: The Board sections (quoted 3-6) have no earlier end than 1970-03-13; the amendment clauses end on 1963-02-22 under their own terms; the surviving sections have no own-terms end. EO 12014 abolished the Board only after those clauses ended.
scope_check: Twelve scopes are decided separately; EO 11515 is a partial amendment (substituting 2(b), striking sections 3-6), not a revocation of the order, and no held source revokes the surviving sections.
independent_command_check: The surviving Medal sections do not depend on the Board: EO 11515 itself kept sections 1 and 2 and removed the Board nomination from 2(b). The self-executing amendments (lead-in, 2(a)) are one-time acts.
savings_check: The surviving sections 1 and 2 continue as amended; the Board sections ended by strike and are not saved; the amendment clauses were exhausted on signing, leaving their product in the amended texts, so no separate savings residual is claimed.

research_rationale: Whole-lifecycle YES claim for EO 12556 (Mailing Privileges of Members of Armed Forces of the United States and of Friendly Foreign Nations, April 16, 1986, 51 FR 13205), read in full from the held Federal Register text. The order has two operative sections and nothing else: section 1 delegates to the Secretary of Defense the function conferred on the President by 39 U.S.C. 3401(a) of designating an area for free mailing privileges, and section 2 requires the Secretary, when performing that function, to consult the Secretary of State, the Postal Service and other agencies and to give the Postal Service timely notice of designations and terminations of designations. Neither section carries a date, a condition, a report deadline or any own-terms end, and the order contains no revocation or supersession of another instrument. No later instrument amending, revoking or superseding the order is held: the packet chain has no events, the later-events OFR catalog search recorded 0 disposition notes naming it, and the held U.S. Code release point 119-121 prints the order's text as a note to 39 U.S.C. 3401 with no ending statement. The underlying statute still gives the President the designation function (held text of 39 U.S.C. 3401(a)(1)), so the delegated function has not lapsed with its authority. The U.S. Code edition is current through 2026-10-09 (laws enacted after that date and on or before 2026-10-14 are not reflected in it); that limit is stated, not filled.
savings_reason: The order remains in force in full; no clause has terminated and the held U.S. Code, packet chain and OFR catalog search show no ending, so no savings or residual effect arises.
earlier_end_check: No earlier end exists: the order has no own-terms end (no date, expiry, condition or sunset), the packet chain lists no later event, and the OFR catalog search found no disposition note. A report or notice requirement is not an end.
scope_check: Section 1 (delegation) and section 2 (consultation and notice) are the only operative sections; each is decided separately. There is no partial revocation or amendment in any held source.
independent_command_check: Section 2 (consult and notify) depends on a function being exercised under section 1; it is a continuing duty of the Secretary of Defense while the delegation stands, not a one-time command, and it has not been performed out of existence because it attaches to each designation or termination.
savings_check: Nothing ended, so there is no residual or savings question: the order and both commands continue; no later instrument is held that could transfer or preserve rights in a savings clause, and the order has none.

research_rationale: Whole-lifecycle YES claim for EO 10717 (The President's Award for Distinguished Federal Civilian Service, June 27, 1957, 22 FR 4632), read in full from the held Federal Register text after correcting the packet inventory (which listed only parts of sections 3 and 9) to the nine original sections. Sections 1 and 2 (the Award and its presentation by the President) remain operative: EO 10979 (1961-12-12) rewrote section 2 and EO 11085 (1963-02-22) amended section 4 and the others conformably, and EO 12014 (1977-10-19) abolished the Distinguished Civilian Service Awards Board and deleted sections 3 to 9, adding new sections 3 and 4 that vest the advisory and nomination functions in the Chairman of the Civil Service Commission. EO 12107 (1978-12-28, effective 1979-01-01) then substituted the Office of Personnel Management for the Civil Service Commission in the added text; it touches none of the original sections inventoried here. Sections 3 to 8 ended on 1977-10-19 by deletion and section 9, a spent effective-date clause, ended on 1957-07-01 under the order's own terms. The held 5 CFR 451.203 shows the Award still operating under EO 10717 as amended (eCFR as of 2026-10-14). The U.S. Code edition is current through 2026-10-09; that limit is stated, not filled.
savings_reason: The order remains in force in part: sections 1 and 2 continue as amended, sections 3 to 9 ended, and the Board functions continue only through the replacement sections added by EO 12014, so no separate savings residual is claimed.
earlier_end_check: Sections 3-8 had no earlier end: the Board continued and was expanded by EO 11085 in 1963 before EO 12014 deleted it; section 9 ended on its own date 1957-07-01. Sections 1 and 2 have no own-terms end and no later deletion. A later general rule (EO 12107) only substitutes agency names in text added after the original sections.
scope_check: Nine original sections are decided separately: the two surviving sections, six deleted Board sections (3-8) and the spent effective-date section. EO 12014 is a partial revocation (deletion of sections 3-9), not a revocation of the order; the packet inventory was corrected because it omitted sections 1 and 2.
independent_command_check: Sections 1 and 2 are independent of the Board sections: the Award exists and is presented by the President without the Board (5 CFR 451.203 shows OPM now makes recommendations). The Board sections were commands about an abolished body, ended together by EO 12014.
savings_check: Sections 1 and 2 continue as amended; the functions of deleted sections 3 to 8 were re-established in new sections added by EO 12014 (outside this inventory) and not saved in the old sections, so no savings or residual effect attaches to the deleted clauses.
